title: Logistics Route Sequencing
business: Regional distribution centers managing high-volume delivery manifests.
problem: Sorting unsorted delivery manifests by destination priority causes significant delays in loading docks, leading to missed transit windows.
solution: Merge Sort provides a stable, predictable sorting mechanism that recursively divides the manifest list into halves, sorts them, and merges the ordered outputs to ensure consistent performance regardless of initial data distribution.
steps: Divide the unsorted manifest list into two equal-sized sub-lists.
Recursively apply the sorting process to each sub-list until individual elements remain.
Compare the elements of the two sub-lists sequentially.
Merge the compared elements back into a single, ordered manifest list.
outcome: Consistent, reliable sorting times for delivery manifests, ensuring loading dock operations remain synchronized with transit schedules.
limitation: Merge Sort requires additional memory proportional to the size of the input list, which can be a constraint in memory-limited embedded hardware; verify memory overhead by monitoring peak heap usage during the merge phase.
